question: What will be the product when CO(g) reacts with H₂ (g) at 340 atm pressure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CH3OH.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When carbon monoxide (CO) reacts with hydrogen gas (H₂) at high pressures, such as 340 atm, the reaction typically produces methanol (CH₃OH). The reaction can be represented as follows: CO(g)+〖2H〗₂ (g) ( 340 atm ) ⃗〖CH〗₃ OH(l)
 
• This reaction is part of the industrial process known as the "Synthesis Gas" or "Syngas" conversion.
 
• The use of methanol as a fuel or fuel additive reduces emissions of particulate matter, CO₂, and other pollutants compared to conventional fossil fuels.
 
• Methanol is used as an antifreeze agent in windshield washer fluid and natural gas pipelines.
